item.text: {"summary":"Restore longest-match precedence for replacements starting at the same position.","explanation":"The latest assertions show one remaining failure group: in ManyReplacements, `s` is `\"xbc\"` instead of `\"xyz\"` for `\"abc\"` with `a`, `ab`, and `abc` candidates; the same ordering issue makes `s` equal `\"Ayz;!\"` instead of `\"Ayz?\"` and leaves shorter-match results in the `\"ababa\"` cases. In VariableNumber, `absl::StrReplaceAll(replacements, &s)` returns 3 instead of 2 and leaves `s` as `\"XXX\"` instead of `\"xX\"` for `\"aaa\"` with `aa` and `a`; the value-returning assertion likewise gets `\"XXXXX\"` instead of `\"xxX\"` for `\"aaaaa\"`. In Inplace, `s` is `\"xbc\"` instead of `\"xyz\"`, and later `reps` counts are too high when longer overlapping matches should win. The cursor in the supplied current implementation already advances by the full matched pattern, so the earlier partial-advance diagnosis does not explain these remaining failures. `OccursBefore` currently treats a shorter candidate at an equal offset as earlier, while the insertion sort places the highest-priority candidate at the back for selection. Reversing the equal-offset size comparison puts the longer candidate there, restoring greedy matching and the substitution counts across overloads.","edits":[{"path":"absl/strings/str_replace.h","old":"    return old.size() < y.old.size();","new":"    return old.size() > y.old.size();"}]}
